settings.assistant.control.option.agents.description: A choice of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.option.look.description: A choice of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.option.projec.description: A choice of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.control.tip.defaultMessage: It never removes agents, discards worktrees or deletes projects, never types into an agent that is working, asking you something or that you just typed in (see Pause after you type), and makes at most 30 changes per message. What it does is listed in its panel. A running Assistant takes a change after a restart.
settings.assistant.control.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): its last paragraph. Pause after you type is another setting: keep its name as Hive shows it.

settings.assistant.control.tip.agents.defaultMessage: Control agents: it can also add agents, change their settings, start and stop them, and give idle ones tasks, when you ask it to. Stopping a busy agent asks you first.
settings.assistant.control.tip.agents.description: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Control agents.

settings.assistant.control.tip.look.defaultMessage: Look and advise: it reads and suggests, and you act.
settings.assistant.control.tip.look.description: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Look and advise.

settings.assistant.control.tip.projects.defaultMessage: Control agents and create projects: also new projects.
settings.assistant.control.tip.projects.description: The info tip of the setting "Control" (Settings → Assistant): a line on the choice Control agents and create projects.

settings.assistant.defaultIs.description: The first choice of a list in Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: what applies when nothing is chosen. {value} says what that is.

settings.assistant.defaultProvider.description: The first choice of Settings → Assistant → Provider: the default provider, and which one that is now.

settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.desc.defaultMessage: Once you press Enter in the terminal (you sent what you typed), the Assistant may type there at once.
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.desc.description: What the setting "Enter ends the pause" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip.defaultMessage: Turn this off if you often type a line and then keep writing (e.g. answering a question, then adding more).
settings.assistant.enterEndsPause.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Enter ends the pause" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.journal.desc.defaultMessage: The Assistant keeps a journal in this workspace: decisions, plans, events and what it learned, recalled a few lines at a time instead of reading a long handover. Hive adds facts: lanes, merges, unexpected closes.
settings.assistant.journal.desc.description: What the setting "Journal" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.journal.tip.defaultMessage: For this workspace. Turning it off keeps the entries; Delete Journal… removes them. The Assistant's journal tools follow a change at its next start; it is told at once.
settings.assistant.journal.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Journal" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.journal.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → Assistant): the Assistant's journal, its memory across sessions.

settings.assistant.panelSide.desc.defaultMessage: Which side of the window the Assistant's panel is on, in every workspace.
settings.assistant.panelSide.desc.description: What the setting "Panel side" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.option.left.description: A choice of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.option.righ.description: A choice of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.panelSide.tip.defaultMessage: On the left it sits between the project list and your work, which keeps it clear of Windows notifications and other windows at the bottom right. View → Move Assistant Panel… and the panel's ⋯ menu switch it too.
settings.assistant.panelSide.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Panel side" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.persona.desc.defaultMessage: How the Assistant works in a new conversation (Coordinator, Planner, QA triager, Release manager, or your own), unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.persona.desc.description: What the setting "Default mode" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.persona.tip.defaultMessage: Modes are Markdown files in each workspace (.hive/personas): edit them, or add your own, in the Hive Assistant view (the robot on the left). The panel switches mode at once, keeping the conversation.
settings.assistant.persona.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Default mode" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.provider.desc.defaultMessage: The coding agent the Assistant runs, unless a workspace chooses another.
settings.assistant.provider.desc.description: What the setting "Provider" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.provider.tip.defaultMessage: The Assistant is independent of your project agents: a Codex Assistant can look after Claude Code agents, and the other way round.
settings.assistant.provider.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Provider" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc.defaultMessage: The Assistant's watch on an agent or its card hears the first line of what you send that agent from its pane.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.desc.description: What the setting "Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip.defaultMessage: So it knows what you told the agent (an answer, a decision) without asking you again, and can record a decision on the card. Only the first line, only to the Assistant of the same workspace, and only when it is watching that agent or its card.
settings.assistant.tellReplies.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.tellReplies.title.defaultMessage: Tell the Assistant when I reply to an agent

settings.assistant.typingPause.desc.defaultMessage: Seconds after you type in an agent's terminal before the Assistant may type there (give it a task or hand its work over).
settings.assistant.typingPause.desc.description: What the setting "Pause after you type" does, under its title (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.typingPause.off.description: The Off box of the number setting "Pause after you type" (Settings → Assistant): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.assistant.typingPause.tip.defaultMessage: The Assistant types a task by clearing the agent's input line (Ctrl+U) and entering it, which would wipe or mix with something you were writing. During the pause it asks you instead.
settings.assistant.typingPause.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Pause after you type" (Settings → Assistant): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.assistant.withProvider.desc.defaultMessage: The model, effort, permission mode{context, select, yes {, context} other {}} and extra arguments when the Assistant runs {provider}. Default follows {provider}'s own settings, except the mode: {mode}, where {provider} approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
settings.assistant.withProvider.desc.description: What the setting "With <provider>" does (Settings → Assistant). {provider} is a coding agent's name, {mode} a permission mode's name; {context} is yes when the provider has a context-size choice.

settings.assistant.withProvider.tip.defaultMessage: By default it uses the same model and effort as your agents. A lighter model or low effort saves tokens but makes it careless (for example, saying it will check on an agent later and never doing so). Its default mode is the one your agents default to, so it rarely asks. Hive's own tools never ask: what they may do is set by Control above.
settings.assistant.withProvider.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "With <provider>" (Settings → Assistant).

settings.assistant.withProvider.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → Assistant): the Assistant's model, effort and mode when it runs this provider. {provider} is a coding agent's name.

settings.assistantDefaults.extraArgsPlac.description: The empty box's placeholder of the setting "Extra arguments". --verbose is an argument: keep it.

settings.assistantProvider.effort.desc.defaultMessage: Its reasoning effort with {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider} → Default effort.
settings.assistantProvider.effort.desc.description: A field of Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: what it is. {provider} is a coding agent's name.

settings.assistantProvider.effort.title.description: A field's title in Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: the Assistant's reasoning effort.

settings.assistantProvider.extraArgs.des.defaultMessage: Additional {cli} command-line arguments when the Assistant runs {provider}.
settings.assistantProvider.extraArgs.des.description: A field of Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: what it is. {provider} is a coding agent's name. {cli} is the CLI's command (claude, codex, copilot): keep it.

settings.assistantProvider.extraArgs.tit.description: A field's title in Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: command-line arguments.

settings.assistantProvider.model.desc.defaultMessage: The model when the Assistant runs {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider} → Default model.
settings.assistantProvider.model.desc.description: A field of Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: what it is. {provider} is a coding agent's name.

settings.assistantProvider.model.title.description: A field's title in Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: the Assistant's model.

settings.assistantProvider.permissionMod.defaultMessage: Its permission mode with {provider}. Empty is {mode}, where {provider} approves safe actions itself and only asks about risky ones.
settings.assistantProvider.permissionMod.description: A field of Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: what it is. {provider} is a coding agent's name. {mode} is a permission mode's name.
A field's title in Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: the Assistant's permission mode.

settings.assistantProvider.use200kContex.defaultMessage: A 200K-token context window for it with {provider}. Empty follows Settings → {provider}.
settings.assistantProvider.use200kContex.description: A field of Settings → Assistant → With <provider>: what it is. {provider} is a coding agent's name.
A field's title in Settings → Assistant → With <provider>. 200K and 1M are numbers of tokens.

settings.board.archiveDoneDays.desc.defaultMessage: Days a card stays in Done before Hive archives it.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.desc.description: What the setting "Archive Done cards after" does, under its title (Settings → Board).

settings.board.archiveDoneDays.off.description: The Off box of the number setting "Archive Done cards after" (Settings → Board): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.board.archiveDoneDays.tip.defaultMessage: Counted from when the card last went into Done (or was brought back from the archive), not from its last change. An archived card is kept: the board's Archived list shows it, and you can bring it back. Hive checks when a workspace opens and every hour.
settings.board.archiveDoneDays.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Archive Done cards after" (Settings → Board): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.board.colors.desc.defaultMessage: Pick the colour of each column.
settings.board.colors.desc.description: What the setting "Column colours" does, under its title (Settings → Board).

settings.board.colors.tip.defaultMessage: The tint on cards is a light mix of the colour with the theme, so it works in light and dark themes. Reset puts back the default.
settings.board.colors.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Column colours" (Settings → Board): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.board.columnColors.desc.defaultMessage: Give each column's heading its colour and tint its cards with it.
settings.board.columnColors.desc.description: What the setting "Colour columns" does, under its title (Settings → Board).

settings.board.columnColors.tip.defaultMessage: A card takes the colour of the column it is in. Blocked, stalled and finished cards keep their red, amber and green edge, and their text, over the tint.
settings.board.columnColors.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Colour columns" (Settings → Board): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.chime.bell.description: A sound of Settings → Notifications → Chime sound.

settings.chime.chime.description: A sound of Settings → Notifications → Chime sound.

settings.chime.play.description: Button beside Settings → Notifications → Chime sound: plays it.

settings.chime.pop.description: A sound of Settings → Notifications → Chime sound.

settings.chime.soft.description: A sound of Settings → Notifications → Chime sound.

settings.columnColors.pick.description: The name, for screen readers, of a board column's colour picker (Settings → Board → Column colours). {column} is the column's name.

settings.columnColors.reset.description: Button beside a board column's colour: puts back its default colour. {column} is the column's name.

settings.data.copied.description: A notice after a path was copied.

settings.data.copyPath.description: Button beside the settings file's path (Settings → Advanced → Settings file): copies it.

settings.emptyDefault.description: In "Reset to default (empty)": the setting's default is empty.

settings.enable.description: Button of the confirmation before a risky setting is turned on.

settings.fallback.add.description: Button under a fallback list: adds the value typed beside it.

settings.fallback.level.description: A column of a provider's fallback list of effort levels: the value Hive passes to the CLI.

settings.fallback.levelPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the box where a new effort level is typed. xhigh is a level's value: keep it.

settings.fallback.levelsPerModel.defaultMessage: {source}: each model offers its own levels; this list names them and is used for models it doesn't describe.
settings.fallback.levelsPerModel.description: Above a provider's fallback list of effort levels, when the CLI reports each model's levels. {source} says where the models come from.

settings.fallback.levelsUsed.defaultMessage: Used now: {provider} hasn't reported per-model levels.
settings.fallback.levelsUsed.description: Above a provider's fallback list of effort levels, when the CLI reports none per model. {provider} is its name.

settings.fallback.modelId.description: A column of a provider's fallback list of models: the ID Hive passes to the CLI.

settings.fallback.modelsNow.description: Above a provider's fallback list of models: where the model pickers' models come from now. {source} says it.

settings.fallback.name.description: A column of a provider's fallback list: the name pickers show.

settings.fallback.nameCell.description: The name, for screen readers, of a row's Name box in a fallback list. {n} is the row's number.

settings.fallback.newLevel.description: The name, for screen readers, of the box under a fallback list of effort levels where a new one is typed.

settings.fallback.newModel.description: The name, for screen readers, of the box under a fallback list of models where a new one is typed.

settings.fallback.older.description: A column of a provider's fallback list of models: ticked, the model is listed under Older models.

settings.fallback.olderCell.description: The name, for screen readers, of a row's Older box in a fallback list. {n} is the row's number.

settings.fallback.remove.description: Button on a row of a fallback list: removes it.

settings.fallback.reset.description: Button under a provider's table (prices, models or effort levels): goes back to Hive's own.

settings.fallback.saveFailed.description: An error's title: saving a provider's fallback list of models or effort levels failed.

settings.fallback.showLevels.defaultMessage: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}})
settings.fallback.showLevels.description: A link that unfolds a provider's fallback list of effort levels. {n} is how many it holds.

settings.fallback.showModels.defaultMessage: Show the list ({n, plural, one {# model} other {# models}})
settings.fallback.showModels.description: A link that unfolds a provider's fallback list of models. {n} is how many it holds.

settings.fallback.valueCell.description: The name, for screen readers, of a box in a fallback list: the column and the row's number.

settings.fileLocks.modeLine.description: A line of the File locks setting's info tip: a mode's name and what it does.

settings.general.closeToTray.desc.defaultMessage: Closing the window keeps Hive running in the system tray so sessions continue.
settings.general.closeToTray.desc.description: What the setting "Close to tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.closeToTray.tip.defaultMessage: When off, closing the window quits Hive (asking first if sessions are running). Use File → Exit or the tray menu to quit.
settings.general.closeToTray.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Close to tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc.defaultMessage: When to ask before quitting stops running sessions.
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.desc.description: What the setting "Confirm before quitting" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.al.description: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.ne.description: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.option.wo.description: A choice of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General).

settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip.defaultMessage: Quitting stops every running session. Their conversations are kept and can be resumed, so by default Hive only asks when an agent is in the middle of something (working, or waiting for your answer).
settings.general.confirmOnQuit.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Confirm before quitting" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.dateFormat.desc.defaultMessage: How dates show in Hive: sessions named by when they started, the session lists and their tooltips, exports.
settings.general.dateFormat.desc.description: What the setting "Date format" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.dmy.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.mdy.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.syste.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.option.ymd.description: A choice of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.dateFormat.tip.defaultMessage: System uses your Windows language's short date. Names you give sessions stay as you typed them: only the automatic ones (when a session started) follow this. How long ago something happened ("2 hours ago") stays, with the date on hover.
settings.general.dateFormat.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Date format" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.keepAwake.desc.defaultMessage: Stop Windows from sleeping while an agent is working or waiting on background tasks, so it doesn't stop mid-task.
settings.general.keepAwake.desc.description: What the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.always.description: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.never.description: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.option.plugge.description: A choice of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General).

settings.general.keepAwake.tip.defaultMessage: Hive lets the PC sleep again as soon as no agent is working. The screen can still turn off and lock. On a laptop, "When plugged in" lets it sleep on battery.
settings.general.keepAwake.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Keep the PC awake while agents work" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.keepAwake.title.defaultMessage: Keep the PC awake while agents work

settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc.defaultMessage: Start Hive automatically when you sign in to Windows.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.desc.description: What the setting "Launch at login" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip.defaultMessage: Hive starts hidden in the tray when launched at login.
settings.general.launchAtLogin.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Launch at login" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc.defaultMessage: Minimising hides Hive to the system tray instead of the taskbar.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.desc.description: What the setting "Minimise to tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip.defaultMessage: Click the tray icon to bring Hive back.
settings.general.minimizeToTray.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Minimise to tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.progressCommands.desc.defaultMessage: Agents run tests, builds and other commands that take more than about 30 seconds through hive-progress without being asked, so they show in the panel. Off: only when you ask.
settings.general.progressCommands.desc.description: What the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.progressCommands.disabl.defaultMessage: Turn on the Progress panel to use this.
settings.general.progressCommands.disabl.description: Under the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" (Settings → General) while the Progress panel is off.

settings.general.progressCommands.tip.defaultMessage: hive-progress runs the command unchanged (same output and exit code). Hive's session guidance tells agents to use it, so a change applies to agents started or restarted afterwards. With the Progress panel off, agents aren't told to use it either.
settings.general.progressCommands.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Agents show long commands in the Progress panel" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.progressCommands.title.defaultMessage: Agents show long commands in the Progress panel

settings.general.progressPanel.desc.defaultMessage: Show long runs agents report, such as tests and builds: how far along each is and the time left, in a panel on the right and on the taskbar button.
settings.general.progressPanel.desc.description: What the setting "Progress panel" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.progressPanel.tip.defaultMessage: Folded, the panel is a strip with a small bar per run; click it, or use Toggle Progress Panel in the command palette. Off hides the panel, the strip and the taskbar progress; agents can still report, and Hive ignores it.
settings.general.progressPanel.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Progress panel" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des.defaultMessage: Open the workspace you used last when Hive starts.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.des.description: What the setting "Reopen last workspace" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip.defaultMessage: Sessions are never resumed automatically — only the workspace is reopened.
settings.general.reopenLastWorkspace.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Reopen last workspace" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.showTips.desc.defaultMessage: One tip a day about something Hive can do, and a tip at the moments one helps.
settings.general.showTips.desc.description: What the setting "Show a tip when Hive starts" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.showTips.tip.defaultMessage: Tips show in a small card in the bottom corner and never get in the way. Help → Tips… lists them all, whether this is on or off.
settings.general.showTips.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Show a tip when Hive starts" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.showTips.title.defaultMessage: Show a tip when Hive starts

settings.general.startMinimized.desc.defaultMessage: Start Hive hidden in the system tray.
settings.general.startMinimized.desc.description: What the setting "Start in tray" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.startMinimized.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Start in tray" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.timeFormat.desc.defaultMessage: How times show with the dates.
settings.general.timeFormat.desc.description: What the setting "Time format" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.option.12h.description: A choice of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.option.24h.description: A choice of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General).

settings.general.timeFormat.tip.defaultMessage: Applies wherever Hive shows a time, such as a session that started today or the time a screenshot was pasted.
settings.general.timeFormat.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Time format" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.general.userName.desc.defaultMessage: How Hive names you to the Hive Assistant when it tells it you replied to an agent ("Darren replied to B1 on #399").
settings.general.userName.desc.description: What the setting "Your name" does, under its title (Settings → General).

settings.general.userName.placeholder.description: The empty box's placeholder of the setting "Your name" (Settings → General).

settings.general.userName.tip.defaultMessage: It goes into the Assistant's conversation, so use whatever form you like it to see. Empty uses "User".
settings.general.userName.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Your name" (Settings → General): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.journal.cap.description: A label before the journal's size limit in MB (Settings → Assistant → Journal).

settings.journal.days.description: After the number of days everyday journal entries are kept.

settings.journal.delete.description: A button: deletes the Assistant's journal of this workspace (asks first). The … says it asks: keep it.

settings.journal.deleteButton.description: Button of the confirmation: deletes the journal.

settings.journal.deleteMessage.defaultMessage: All {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} of this workspace go to the Recycle Bin. The Assistant starts again with an empty journal.
settings.journal.deleteMessage.description: The question before the journal is deleted; {entries} is how many entries it has. Recycle Bin is Windows' name for it.

settings.journal.deleteTitle.description: Title of the question before the Assistant's journal is deleted.

settings.journal.deleted.description: A notice after the Assistant's journal was deleted.

settings.journal.failed.description: An error's title: saving the journal settings or deleting the journal failed (why follows).

settings.journal.kind.decision.description: A kind of entry the Assistant may keep in its journal (Settings → Assistant → Journal): what was decided.

settings.journal.kind.event.description: A kind of journal entry: what happened (Hive records lanes, merges and unexpected closes as events too).

settings.journal.kind.incident.description: A kind of journal entry: something that went wrong.

settings.journal.kind.insight.description: A kind of journal entry: something learned.

settings.journal.kind.moment.description: A kind of journal entry: a memorable moment of working together. Off by default.

settings.journal.kind.plan.description: A kind of journal entry: what is planned.

settings.journal.kind.preference.description: A kind of journal entry: how the user likes things done. Off by default.

settings.journal.local.defaultMessage: Kept on this computer only, in .hive/assistant/journal.db, and never sent anywhere.
settings.journal.local.description: A note under the journal settings (privacy). Keep the file path as it is.

settings.journal.mb.defaultMessage: MB (past it, the oldest everyday entries go first)
settings.journal.mb.description: After the journal's size limit in megabytes.

settings.journal.noLimit.description: A checkbox: the journal has no size limit.

settings.journal.noWorkspace.defaultMessage: Open a workspace to set its Assistant's journal.
settings.journal.noWorkspace.description: Settings → Assistant → Journal with no workspace open.

settings.journal.none.description: The journal before the Assistant or Hive has written anything.

settings.journal.offKeeps.defaultMessage: Off, nothing is written and the Assistant's journal tools go at its next start; the entries are kept.
settings.journal.offKeeps.description: Under the journal switch when it is off.

settings.journal.on.description: A switch (Settings → Assistant → Journal): the Assistant keeps a journal in this workspace. Off keeps what is there.

settings.journal.retention.description: A label before a number of days (Settings → Assistant → Journal). Digests and important entries are kept longer.

settings.journal.scope.description: A heading (Settings → Assistant → Journal): the kinds of entries the Assistant may keep.

settings.journal.size.defaultMessage: Now {size}, {entries, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}}.
settings.journal.size.description: The journal's size on disk ({size}: "1.2 MB") and how many entries it has.

settings.keybindings.editor.desc.defaultMessage: Click the pencil (or double-click a shortcut), then press the new keys. Wait a moment after the first combination, or press a second one for a chord such as Ctrl+K Ctrl+S.
settings.keybindings.editor.desc.description: What the setting "Shortcuts" does, under its title (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts).

settings.keybindings.editor.tip.defaultMessage: Shortcuts need Ctrl or Alt (or are F-keys). Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y and Shift+Tab stay with editing and the agents' terminals. Some keys go to the agent while its terminal has focus (for Claude Code: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+G).
settings.keybindings.editor.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Shortcuts" (Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.keys.alsoUsed.description: Tooltip of the warning beside a shortcut other commands use too. {commands} lists them.

settings.sessions.defaultView.desc.description: What the setting "Default session view" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions). Panes and Tiles are the toggle's choices: use their translations.

settings.sessions.defaultView.option.pan.description: A choice of the setting "Default session view" (Settings → Sessions): the agents' terminals in panes. Use the Panes | Tiles toggle's word.

settings.sessions.defaultView.option.til.description: A choice of the setting "Default session view" (Settings → Sessions): a small tile per agent. Use the Panes | Tiles toggle's word.

settings.sessions.defaultView.tip.defaultMessage: Panes shows each agent's terminal; Tiles shows each agent as a small tile, so a whole team fits on one screen. A project remembers its own choice once you use its toggle, so changing this only affects projects that haven't chosen yet.
settings.sessions.defaultView.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Default session view" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.followTranscripts.desc.defaultMessage: The Sessions tab shows new messages of a running session as they arrive.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.desc.description: What the setting "Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.followTranscripts.tip.defaultMessage: Off: the transcript shows what was there when you opened it; Refresh loads what is new. You can also switch following on in the viewer itself. The Session tab always shows the agent working.
settings.sessions.followTranscripts.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.followTranscripts.titl.defaultMessage: Follow running sessions in the transcript viewer

settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.desc.defaultMessage: How the Overview and the session lists update while agents work.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.desc.description: What the setting "Overview updates" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.option.description: A choice of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions).
A choice of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.tip.defaultMessage: Live updates as sessions change, at most every 15 seconds and only while the tab is shown. Each update reads the project's session files, so with many sessions or agents a slower choice keeps Hive lighter. Refresh always updates at once.
settings.sessions.overviewRefresh.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Overview updates" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.recordPerformance.desc.defaultMessage: Count what Hive's Agent API, tools, guidance and skills cost, for the Performance view.
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.desc.description: What the setting "Record performance metrics" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.recordPerformance.tip.defaultMessage: Only totals are kept: request and reply sizes, times and outcomes, the size of what each session was given, and the providers' own reported usage. Never prompts, replies, tokens or paths. Kept 30 days per workspace in .hive/metrics (git-ignored, this machine's). Turned off, nothing new is recorded; what was recorded stays until you reset it.
settings.sessions.recordPerformance.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Record performance metrics" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.resetPerformance.desc.defaultMessage: Clear this workspace's recorded performance metrics.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.desc.description: What the setting "Reset performance metrics" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.resetPerformance.tip.defaultMessage: Starts the history again from now. Session usage and transcripts are not affected.
settings.sessions.resetPerformance.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Reset performance metrics" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.defaultMessage: When Hive closed without quitting (a crash, or it was ended), resume the agents that were running when it starts again.
settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.description: What the setting "Resume agents after an unexpected close" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.defaultMessage: Off: Hive only tells you, with Resume All for you to choose. Either way the notice says when Hive was last seen and which agents were running.
settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.description: The info tip of the setting "Resume agents after an unexpected close" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.resumeAfterUnexpectedC.defaultMessage: Resume agents after an unexpected close

settings.sessions.tileOrder.desc.defaultMessage: The order of the agents' tiles in the Tiles view.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.desc.description: What the setting "Tile order" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.tileOrder.option.panes.description: A choice of the setting "Tile order" (Settings → Sessions): the tiles in the panes' order. The default.

settings.sessions.tileOrder.option.urgen.description: A choice of the setting "Tile order" (Settings → Sessions): waiting for you and stalled first, then working, then idle.

settings.sessions.tileOrder.tip.defaultMessage: Same as panes keeps the agents in their panes' order, so a builder stays beside its reviewer: tiles waiting for you or stalled are highlighted where they are, and a page button counts them on other pages. By urgency puts them first, then the agents working, then the idle ones.
settings.sessions.tileOrder.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Tile order" (Settings → Sessions). "Same as panes" and "By urgency" are its choices: use their translations.

settings.sessions.tileOrder.title.description: A setting's title (Settings → Sessions): the order of the Tiles view's tiles.

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.desc.defaultMessage: Size, in MB, at which a running conversation's transcript turns orange in its footer and Hive notifies you once.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.desc.description: What the setting "Warn when a transcript is over" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.off.description: The Off box of the number setting "Warn when a transcript is over" (Settings → Sessions): ticked, the setting is off (0).

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.tip.defaultMessage: A long conversation slows down the CLI and Hive: each turn, resume and transcript view has more to read. Compacting doesn't shrink the file, which keeps the whole history; handing the work over to a new conversation does (click the size in the footer for Hand Over to…, and choose the agent itself). Projects can set their own value in Project Settings.
settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Warn when a transcript is over" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.transcriptWarnMB.title.defaultMessage: Warn when a transcript is over

settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.desc.defaultMessage: Forget what the cache holds; each transcript is read again the next time it is shown.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.desc.description: What the setting "Clear the usage cache" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.tip.defaultMessage: Only needed if the token counts look wrong. Nothing else is lost: sessions, transcripts and backups stay as they are.
settings.sessions.usageCacheClear.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Clear the usage cache" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.desc.defaultMessage: How many transcripts Hive remembers the token use of, so the Overview and session lists open without reading them again, also after a restart.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.desc.description: What the setting "Usage cache size" does, under its title (Settings → Sessions).

settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.tip.defaultMessage: Kept in usage-cache.json in your Hive profile: a few KB per transcript. A transcript is read again only when it changed (for example, a session you continued outside Hive), and the cache starts afresh with each Hive version. The least recently used go first when it is full. {min, number} to {max, number}.
settings.sessions.usageCacheSize.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Usage cache size" (Settings → Sessions): more on what it does and when it applies. {min} and {max} are the fewest and most transcripts it can be set to.

settings.token.copied.description: A notice after a token was copied.

settings.token.copy.description: Button beside a token: copies it.

settings.token.hide.description: Button beside a token: hides it again.

settings.token.regenerate.description: Button beside the Agent API's token: makes a new one.

settings.token.regenerateMessage.defaultMessage: Programs using the current token will stop working. Running sessions pick up the new token when restarted.
settings.token.regenerateMessage.description: The question before the Agent API's token is replaced.

settings.token.regenerateTitle.description: Title of the question before the Agent API's token is replaced.

settings.token.show.description: Button beside a hidden token: shows it.

settings.updates.checkAutomatically.desc.defaultMessage: Look for a new version of Hive shortly after it starts and every 6 hours.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.desc.description: What the setting "Check for updates automatically" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.checkAutomatically.tip.defaultMessage: When off, Hive only checks when you choose Help → Check for Updates…; development builds never update.
settings.updates.checkAutomatically.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Check for updates automatically" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.d.defaultMessage: Download a new version in the background as soon as it is found.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.d.description: What the setting "Download updates automatically" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.t.defaultMessage: When off, the status bar says a new version is available and you choose when to download it. Downloads are checked against the release checksum.
settings.updates.downloadAutomatically.t.description: The info tip of the setting "Download updates automatically" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.install.desc.defaultMessage: When a downloaded update is installed.
settings.updates.install.desc.description: What the setting "Install updates" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.install.option.auto.description: A choice of the setting "Install updates" (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.install.option.manual.description: A choice of the setting "Install updates" (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.install.tip.defaultMessage: Automatically: the update installs when you next quit Hive (never while it is running, so your sessions are not interrupted); Restart and Update installs it straight away. Manually: it installs only when you choose Restart and Update. Either way, Hive asks before stopping agents that are working.
settings.updates.install.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Install updates" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.prerelease.desc.defaultMessage: Also offer beta versions published before a full release.
settings.updates.prerelease.desc.description: What the setting "Include pre-releases" does, under its title (Settings → Updates).

settings.updates.prerelease.tip.defaultMessage: Pre-releases get new features first and may have rough edges. Turning this off again waits for the next full release rather than going back.
settings.updates.prerelease.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Include pre-releases" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.updates.status.tip.defaultMessage: The version you are running and the result of the last check.
settings.updates.status.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Hive Desktop version" (Settings → Updates): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.usageCache.clear.description: Button of Settings → Sessions → Clear the usage cache.

settings.usageCache.clearFailed.defaultMessage: Could not clear the usage cache
settings.usageCache.clearFailed.description: An error's title: clearing the usage cache failed.

settings.usageCache.cleared.description: A notice after Settings → Sessions → Clear the usage cache.

settings.usageCache.clearedDetail.defaultMessage: Each transcript is read again the next time it is shown.
settings.usageCache.clearedDetail.description: More in the notice after the usage cache was cleared.

settings.viewers.made.description: A notice after a viewer token was made (Settings → Agent API → Viewer tokens). {name} is the name the user gave it.

settings.viewers.madeColumn.description: A column of the viewer tokens table: when the token was made.

settings.viewers.madeDetail.defaultMessage: Copy it into the app it is for.
settings.viewers.madeDetail.description: More in the notice after a viewer token was made.

settings.viewers.make.description: Button: makes a viewer token with the name typed beside it.

settings.viewers.makeFailed.defaultMessage: Could not make the viewer token
settings.viewers.makeFailed.description: An error's title: making a viewer token failed.

settings.viewers.name.description: A column of the viewer tokens table: the name the user gave a token.

settings.viewers.nameLabel.description: The name, for screen readers, of the box where a new viewer token's name is typed.

settings.viewers.namePlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the box where a new viewer token's name is typed. Apiary is an app's name: keep it.

settings.viewers.revokeFailed.defaultMessage: Could not revoke the viewer token
settings.viewers.revokeFailed.description: An error's title: revoking a viewer token failed.

settings.viewers.revokeMessage.defaultMessage: The app using it can no longer read Hive, and its event stream ends now.
settings.viewers.revokeMessage.description: The question before a viewer token is revoked.

settings.viewers.revokeTitle.description: Title of the question before a viewer token is revoked. {name} is its name.

settings.viewers.token.description: A column of the viewer tokens table: the token.

settings.viewers.tokenOf.description: The name, for screen readers, of a viewer token's box. {name} is the token's name.

settings.workspace.antivirus.desc.defaultMessage: Whether Microsoft Defender scans the workspace's folders as Hive's work changes them (builds, tests, git, worktrees), and the exclusions Hive can add for them, with your consent.
settings.workspace.antivirus.desc.description: What the setting "Antivirus scanning" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.antivirus.tip.defaultMessage: Hive checks without administrator rights, so Defender may not show its exclusions (unknown). Adding or removing exclusions asks for administrator rights once. Hive only ever offers these folders: the workspace, its worktrees folder once it exists, and its test area for people developing Hive. It never changes other antivirus products.
settings.workspace.antivirus.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Antivirus scanning" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.desc.defaultMessage: Restore one to bring it back with its cards (and, for a removed one, the handovers packed into its folder). A folder that has left the workspace can be forgotten.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.desc.description: What the setting "Hidden and removed projects" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.tip.defaultMessage: Project → Remove Project… hides a project, removes it from Hive (its folder keeps its handovers and cards in .hive/removed, so it can move to another workspace) or deletes it (to the Recycle Bin). Deleted projects are not listed here: restore the folder from the Recycle Bin and Hive sees it as a new project.
settings.workspace.hiddenProjects.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Hidden and removed projects" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workspace.loopRounds.desc.defaultMessage: How many rounds a card gets in a card loop (a build and its review each) before its agents stop and ask you, when you don't say. Projects can set their own.
settings.workspace.loopRounds.desc.description: What the setting "Card loop rounds" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.loopRounds.tip.defaultMessage: Saying "rounds: 5" when you start a loop still wins. Agents read this when they register the loop (its lane), so a change applies to loops started afterwards.
settings.workspace.loopRounds.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Card loop rounds" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.desc.defaultMessage: How many hours an agent in a card loop waits with no change before it tells you, when you don't say. Projects can set their own.
settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.desc.description: What the setting "Card loop wait" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.tip.defaultMessage: Saying "wait: 2h" when you start a loop still wins. Up to a day. Agents read this when they register the loop (its lane), so a change applies to loops started afterwards.
settings.workspace.loopWaitHours.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Card loop wait" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.

settings.workspace.storage.desc.defaultMessage: What Hive keeps for each of the workspace's projects (the biggest first) and the Hive Assistant: transcript backups, archived sessions, attachments and worktrees. Storage opens a project's page, with Clean Up….
settings.workspace.storage.desc.description: What the setting "Storage" does, under its title (Settings → Workspace).

settings.workspace.storage.tip.defaultMessage: Measured in the background, a project at a time. The coding agents' own transcripts (in ~/.claude and ~/.codex) aren't counted. Hidden projects aren't included.
settings.workspace.storage.tip.description: The info tip of the setting "Storage" (Settings → Workspace): more on what it does and when it applies.
